title: Shadow traffic: safety warnings, retention callouts, and sampling/cost UX copy
creator: Kenji Nakamura
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
description:
Goal
Define and deliver Console copy + warning patterns for Shadow Experiments that:
- Sets correct expectations: shadow traffic does NOT affect user responses, but can increase compute/telemetry spend.
- Communicates data handling clearly: what is captured, how it’s redacted, retention defaults, and what admins can configure.
- Guides safe sampling choices: recommended defaults, cost estimate UX, and guardrails to prevent accidental spend or operational risk.

Scope (this ticket)
1) UX copy + warnings across the Shadow Experiments creation flow
- “Create Shadow Experiment” page
- “Review & Start” step
- In-product banner(s) on first enablement / first run
- Results page callouts (interpreting deltas + data limitations)

2) Data retention & sensitive data callouts
- Plain-language explanation of captured artifacts (request metadata, prompts/contexts, candidate outputs)
- Redaction/minimization caveats
- Retention defaults and where to change them (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Role/permission requirements (who can view sampled examples)

3) Sampling rate + cost UX
- Inline explanation of sampling options (percent + deterministic bucketing)
- Recommended “safe start” suggestion
- Estimated incremental cost presentation (telemetry + scoring)
- Warnings when configurations exceed thresholds (e.g., sampling too high, too many shadow targets)

Non-goals
- Writing the full docs page (tracked separately by DevEx); this ticket is Console copy + pattern language.
- Legal/compliance policy text; we link to policy docs where needed and keep Console copy product-focused.

Proposed warning / callout patterns
A) First-time enablement warning (modal or banner)
Title: “Shadow traffic increases cost and may store additional data”
Body:
- “Shadow traffic mirrors a sampled subset of production requests to one or more candidate variants. Users still receive responses from your control variant.”
- “Mirroring can increase GPU usage and evaluation/scoring costs.”
- “Depending on your settings, prompts/contexts and model outputs may be stored for a limited time for scoring and debugging. Apply redaction and review retention before enabling for sensitive routes.”
Buttons:
- Primary: “Review settings”
- Secondary: “Enable with recommended defaults”
- Tertiary: “Cancel”
Footer link: “Learn about retention & redaction” (links to Console retention settings + docs)

B) Inline warning when selecting shadow targets
If >1 shadow target selected:
- “Each additional shadow target multiplies mirrored traffic and scoring costs.”
If shadow target is in a different region:
- “Cross-region mirroring may increase data transfer and may be restricted by residency settings.”

C) Sampling rate control copy
Control label: “Shadow sampling rate”
Helper text:
- “Percentage of requests mirrored to shadow targets. Mirrored requests never change the user response.”
- “We use deterministic bucketing to keep comparisons stable over time.”
Default recommendation (beta): 0.5% (or 1% depending on PM/SRE signoff)
Suggested helper: “Start low (0.1–1%) and increase after validating overhead and signal quality.”

D) Cost estimate box (right rail or inline)
Header: “Estimated incremental cost”
Line items (copy-level; exact numbers come from backend):
- “Mirrored inference (shadow targets)”
- “Scoring & evaluation”
- “Telemetry storage”
Footnote:
- “Estimates are based on the last 24h traffic for this route and may vary with prompt length, output length, and scoring configuration.”
Warning state if estimation unavailable:
- “Cost estimate unavailable (insufficient recent traffic). Start with 0.1% sampling.”

E) Data handling / retention callout (Review & Start step)
Title: “Data handling”
Body bullets:
- “By default, shadow artifacts are minimized and retained for a short period for scoring and investigation.”
- “Enable redaction to remove sensitive fields from prompts/contexts before storage.”
- “Viewing sampled examples requires elevated permissions.”
CTA links:
- “Configure retention & redaction”
- “View audit logging settings”

F) Results page caveats (quality deltas interpretation)
Callout: “Interpreting deltas”
- “Quality metrics are computed on a sampled subset of traffic. Use confidence intervals to assess significance.”
- “A change in output length/verbosity can shift some rubric scores; review examples before rolling back.”
- “If scoring is delayed, metrics may lag behind latency/cost charts.”

Copy drafts (v0) by UI surface
1) Create Shadow Experiment (top-of-page explainer)
“Shadow experiments let you measure quality changes during rollouts by mirroring a sampled subset of requests to candidate variants. Users still receive the control response.”

2) Route selection tooltip
“Shadow traffic mirrors requests after routing decisions. If a request fails over, the shadow assignment follows the final control variant.”

3) “Shadow targets” section helper
“Shadow targets receive mirrored requests for comparison only. Shadow responses are not returned to users.”

4) Sampling slider tooltip
“Sampling is applied deterministically per request fingerprint. The same request pattern will consistently bucket into control/shadow to reduce variance.”

5) Examples access warning (results drilldown)
“Sampled prompts and outputs may contain sensitive information. Limit access to trusted team members.”

6) Kill switch guidance (inline link to runbook)
“Need to stop shadowing quickly? Disable the experiment or set sampling to 0%. Shadow traffic is fail-open and should not impact user responses.”

Open questions (needs PM/SRE/Security input)
1) Default sampling recommendation for beta: 0.1% vs 0.5% vs 1% (depends on scoring cost + statistical power targets).
2) Do we allow starting without cost estimate, or require estimate to be present above a certain sampling rate?
3) Dedicated/Private wording: do we present different retention defaults by deployment mode in-line, or via a “Learn more” drawer?
4) Permissions naming: what are final RBAC labels for “view examples” vs “view aggregates”?
5) Residency restrictions: what exact error copy should appear if cross-region mirroring is blocked by policy?

Acceptance criteria
- Copy approved by Product (Marissa Cole) and reviewed by Security (Marcus Lin / Naomi Feldman) for correctness and non-overpromising on redaction.
- SRE review (Sean Gallagher) confirms warning thresholds align with guardrails (sampling limits, shadow target count, scoring lag).
- Design specs delivered to engineering with:
  - Final strings (or near-final) for primary surfaces
  - Clear rules for when warnings appear (conditions)
  - Guidance for “recommended defaults” button behavior
- Content matches the overall Console tone: concise, developer-first, avoids fear-mongering but is explicit about cost/data.
